generators.carrier: For a listing [x1,...,xn] of P and a family A : P -> Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) Q, returns A_x1 * ... * A_xn, i.e. the list product of the mapped list
Swaps positions i and i+1 of a linear extension; it is defined only when the two elements are incomparable (spacelike), so the result is again a linear extension

relations.statement: ordered_product(adjacent_swap(L,i), A) = ordered_product(L, A) whenever A_{L_i} * A_{L_{i+1}} = A_{L_{i+1}} * A_{L_i}
relations.hypotheses: L_i and L_{i+1} are incomparable in P; A commutes on spacelike pairs

relations.statement: Any two linear extensions of a finite strict poset are connected by a finite chain of adjacent swaps of incomparable elements
relations.hypotheses: P is a finite strict partial order

relations.statement: For the Pauli matrices, X*Z = -(Z*X). So swapping two spacelike elements that carry X and Z negates the ordered product
relations.hypotheses: A_x = X and A_y = Z with x,y incomparable

lemmas.statement: In any monoid, if a*b = b*a then (l1 ++ a :: b :: l2).prod = (l1 ++ b :: a :: l2).prod. This is the elementary swap lemma for general n
lemmas.lean_skeleton:
theorem list_prod_adjacent_swap {M : Type*} [Monoid M] (l₁ l₂ : List M) (a b : M) (h : a * b = b * a) : (l₁ ++ a :: b :: l₂).prod = (l₁ ++ b :: a :: l₂).prod := by
  simp only [List.prod_append, List.prod_cons]
  rw [← mul_assoc a b, h, mul_assoc]

lemmas.statement: For a finite strict poset P and A : P -> Matrix with A x * A y = A y * A x for all incomparable x,y, any two linear extensions L, L' satisfy (L.map A).prod = (L'.map A).prod
lemmas.lean_skeleton:
theorem ordered_product_linext_invariant {P : Type*} [PartialOrder P] [Fintype P] {d : ℕ} (A : P → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℚ) (hA : ∀ x y, ¬ x ≤ y → ¬ y ≤ x → A x * A y = A y * A x) (L L' : List P) (hL : L.Nodup ∧ (∀ x, x ∈ L) ∧ L.Sorted (fun x y => ¬ y < x)) (hL' : L'.Nodup ∧ (∀ x, x ∈ L') ∧ L'.Sorted (fun x y => ¬ y < x)) : (L.map A).prod = (L'.map A).prod := by
  sorry

near_misses.claim: BornFable.OrderedQUnit.linear_extension (lean4/BornLinearExtension.lean) proves the poset linear-extension statement
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: That theorem extends an effect valuation to a Q-linear functional on an order-unit space. It shares only the name 'linear extension' and has nothing to do with listings of a poset, so it cannot license any step here

near_misses.claim: The ordered product is independent of the linear extension even when spacelike elements carry anticommuting matrices
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: On the antichain {x,y} with A_x = X and A_y = Z, the two linear extensions give XZ and ZX = -XZ, and XZ is nonzero. The products differ by the sign -1

near_misses.claim: The finite lemma is the Epstein-Glaser causal factorization
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: It is only an analogy. The distribution extension and the UV content have no finite counterpart
